---
title: "EvoDAG"
subtitle: "Evolving Directed Acyclic Graphs: semantic genetic programming for classification and regression"
---

EvoDAG is a Python library that learns a classifier or a regressor with
genetic programming. It keeps every individual it ever creates in a table,
and each one is a node of a directed acyclic graph that points at the nodes
it was built from. The result of a run is not a tree but a small graph in
which many nodes share the same inputs.

What sets it apart from textbook genetic programming is how a new
individual is made. Every individual is described by its *semantics*, the
vector of values it produces on the training examples. When a function
(a sum, a product, a Naive Bayes classifier, ...) combines existing
individuals, EvoDAG also fits the coefficients of the combination by
ordinary least squares so that the result is as close as possible to the
target vector. The genetic operator therefore acts at the root of the new
individual, and only the examples (not the whole expression) are evaluated.
The [How it works](pages/how-it-works.qmd) page walks through the method.

You use it like any other estimator: `fit(X, y)` and `predict(X)`. A single
run can overfit, so the usual way to use EvoDAG is an ensemble of
independent runs, each one stopped early on its own validation split. A
command line interface (`EvoDAG-params`, `EvoDAG-train`, `EvoDAG-predict`
and `EvoDAG-utils`) covers the same ground for people who prefer to work
with files.

## A first example

The snippet below trains an ensemble of five models on a small synthetic
problem and predicts the training set. It is deliberately tiny so that it
runs in a few seconds; the real defaults use much larger populations (see
[Parameters](pages/parameters.qmd)).

```python
import numpy as np
from EvoDAG import EvoDAGE

rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
X = rng.randn(200, 4)
y = (X[:, 0] + X[:, 1] ** 2 > 1).astype(int)

model = EvoDAGE(n_estimators=5, n_jobs=1, popsize=100,
                early_stopping_rounds=100, seed=0).fit(X, y)
hy = model.predict(X)
print("accuracy on the training set:", (hy == y).mean())
```
